questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic manifest linting and security checks in CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes manifests
- YAML parsing with yq
- GitHub Actions gating
- SecurityContext and imagePullPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-manifest-gate.yml
name: Manifest Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate manifests
        run: |
          set -e
          violations=0
          for f in $(git diff --name-only origin/main | grep -E '\\.ya?ml$' ); do
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].readinessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].livenessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsNonRoot' "$f" | grep -q true; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsUser' "$f" | grep -q '1000'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].imagePullPolicy' "$f" | grep -q 'Always'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
          done
          if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing.yaml (no readiness/liveness probes or runAsNonRoot)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bad-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

```yaml
# passing.yaml (probes present, non-root, Always)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: good-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 80
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 80
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this gate to cover initContainers?
- How would you surface violations to developers (e.g., PR checks, annotated reviews)?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce cross-cloud data provenance and model lineage for ML workloads; ensures reproducibility and auditing of deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- Image digests, internal registries, provenance annotations
- MLflow tracking integration and run_id propagation
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Fail
  rules:
  - name: require-provenance-annotations
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Missing provenance annotations: model_version, dataset_hash, training_run_id'
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            model_version: '*'
            dataset_hash: '*'
            training_run_id: '*'
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Container image must include a digest'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '*@*'
```

```yaml
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-fail
  annotations:
    model_version: v1

  replicas: 1

    metadata:
```

```yaml
    training_run_id: tr-789

  replicas: 1

      containers:
      - name: predictor

```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests designing end-to-end security controls across CI and runtime in a multi-cloud Kubernetes environment, combining image signing, registry governance, and host attestation. 

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore/cosign image signing and Rekor attestations
- OPA/Gatekeeper policy constraints for manifests
- Digest pinning and registry allowlists
- TPM/attestation-based runtime scheduling
- End-to-end CI validation and production-time checks

## Code Example
```javascript
// Minimal Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate for image signature
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: K8sImageSig
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageSig
        listKind: K8sImageSigList
        plural: k8simagesigs
        singular: k8simagesig
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8simagesig
        violation["image unsigned"] {
          input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
          image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
          not image.endswith("@sha256:")
        }
```

- How would you handle edge cases like multi- tenant imaging workflows or private registries?

## Why This Is Asked

Immutability of container images is a core security practice. This checks a tangible gating mechanism candidates can implement in a simple CI step.

## Key Concepts

- YAML manifest parsing
- Image digest pinning (immutable refs)
- Lightweight CI scripts in GitHub Actions
- Local verification parity with CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This evaluates the ability to translate security requirements into automated validation for Helm-rendered Kubernetes manifests, demonstrating practical DevOps security implementation skills.

## Key Concepts

- Helm template rendering for manifest generation
- Kubernetes container securityContext enforcement
- GitHub Actions as CI/CD security gates
- Lightweight YAML validation using shell scripting

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Helm Security Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'charts/**'
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-helm@v3
      - name: Render and validate security context
        run: |
          helm template myapp charts/myapp > rendered.yaml
          # Validate security context fields
          python3 scripts/validate-security.py rendered.yaml
```

```python
# scripts/validate-security.py
import sys, yaml
with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
    docs = yaml.safe_load_all(f)
for doc in docs:
    if doc.get('kind') == 'Deployment':
        for container in doc['spec']['template']['spec']['containers']:
            ctx = container.get('securityContext', {})
            if not ctx.get('runAsNonRoot'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing runAsNonRoot")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('runAsUser', 0) >= 1000:
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} runAsUser < 1000")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('readOnlyRootFilesystem'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing readOnlyRootFilesystem")
                sys.exit(1)
print("All security context checks passed")
```

```yaml
# Failing Helm template - missing readOnlyRootFilesystem
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          # readOnlyRootFilesystem: true  # Missing - will fail CI
```

```yaml
# Passing Helm template - complete security context
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Verification

**Local testing:**
```bash
helm template myapp charts/myapp | python3 scripts/validate-security.py -
```

**CI verification:** The GitHub Actions workflow runs automatically on pull requests, rendering templates and validating security context fields before allowing merge.

## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

### Follow-up
- Extend to handle missing tests per service gracefully
- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical DevOps security skills by testing your ability to implement automated security gates that prevent secret leakage and ensure deployment consistency, directly connecting code hygiene to CI/CD workflows.

## Key Concepts
- Secret scanning integration in CI pipelines
- Baseline management for handling false positives
- Comprehensive coverage of manifests and Helm values
- Local development vs CI environment verification
- Image tag approval and enforcement workflows
- Automated security gates in pull request processes

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions CI Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Secret Scan & Image Validation
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
      - '**/values.yaml'
      - '**/Chart.yaml'

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install detect-secrets
        run: pip install detect-secrets

      - name: Scan for secrets
        run: |
          # Initialize baseline if it doesn't exist
          if [ ! -f .secrets.baseline ]; then
            detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline
          fi
          
          # Run scan and fail if new secrets detected
          detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline --all-files
          
          # Check for any high-entropy results
          if detect-secrets audit --report .secrets.baseline | grep -q "High Entropy"; then
            echo "❌ Secrets detected! Please review and remove before merging."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate image tags
        run: |
          # Define approved tags (in production, store this securely)
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest"
          
          # Extract image tags from manifests
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" | \
            sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://' | \
            sort -u > /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          # Validate each tag
          while IFS= read -r tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag '$tag' is not in approved list: $APPROVED_TAGS"
              exit 1
            fi
          done < /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          echo "✅ All image tags are approved"

      - name: Comment on PR (if failed)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: '🚨 **Security Scan Failed**\n\nThis PR contains either hardcoded secrets or unapproved image tags. Please review the failed job and fix the issues before merging.'
            })
```

### Example Manifest That Would Fail
```yaml
# deployment-with-secrets.yaml (THIS WOULD FAIL THE SCAN)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webapp
        # ❌ Unapproved image tag - will fail validation
        image: myregistry/webapp:v1.3.0-beta
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        env:
        # ❌ Hardcoded secret - will fail scanning
        - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
          value: "super-secret-password-12345"
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "AKIA1234567890ABCDEFGHI"
        # ❌ Another high-entropy string
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          value: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ"
```

### Configuration Files

#### detect-secrets Configuration
```yaml
# .detect-secrets.yml
version: "0.14"
plugins:
  - name: ArtifactoryDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.artifactory
  - name: AWSKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.aws
  - name: Base64HighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "base64"
      min_entropy: 4.5  # Adjust for false positives
  - name: HexHighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "hex"
      min_entropy: 3.0
  - name: KeywordDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.keyword
    keyword_exclude: "passkey,password"  # Add safe keywords
  - name: PrivateKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.private_key
  - name: SlackTokenDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.slack

filters:
  - detect_secrets.filters.common.is_likely_id_string
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_indented_comment
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_potential_uuid
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_sequential_string

# Paths to exclude from scanning
exclude_files:
  - "tests/.*\.mock\.yaml$"
  - "docs/.*\.md$"
```

#### Pre-commit Hook Configuration
```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: detect-secrets
        args: ['--baseline', '.secrets.baseline']
  
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: validate-image-tags
        name: Validate image tags
        entry: bash -c '
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest" &&
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" |
          sed "s/.*:\s*//" | sed "s/\"//g" | sed "s/.*://" |
          sort -u | while read tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag \"$tag\" is not approved"
              exit 1
            fi
          done'
        language: system
        files: \.(yaml|yml)$
```

## Local Verification Steps

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
# Install detect-secrets
pip install detect-secrets

# Install pre-commit hooks
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

### 2. Initial Setup
```bash
# Create initial baseline
find . -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" | xargs detect-secrets scan > .secrets.baseline

# Review and audit the baseline
detect-secrets audit .secrets.baseline
```

### 3. Test the Workflow
```bash
# Test with a problematic file (should fail)
cat > test-bad.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-secret
data:
  password: c3VwZXItc2VjcmV0LXBhc3N3b3JkLTEyMzQ1  # base64 encoded secret
EOF

# Run the scan (should fail)
detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline test-bad.yaml

# Clean up
rm test-bad.yaml
```

### 4. Test Image Tag Validation
```bash
# Create deployment with unapproved tag
cat > test-deployment.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v2.0.0  # Not in approved list
EOF

# This should fail the image tag validation
grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" | sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://'

rm test-deployment.yaml
```

## How to Verify in CI

1. **Push a test PR** with problematic files to your fork
2. **Check GitHub Actions** tab to see the security scan job
3. **Verify the job fails** when secrets or unapproved tags are detected
4. **Fix the issues** and push again to confirm the job passes
5. **Review PR comments** for automated notifications when scans fail

## Best Practices

- Store approved image tags in a config file or secret management system
- Use semantic versioning for image tags
- Implement secret management (Kubernetes Secrets, Vault, etc.)
- Regularly update the baseline after auditing
- Enable dependency scanning for container images
- Use image signing and verification for production deployments

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests practical, auditable governance for multi-team clusters beyond image/security gates.

Key Concepts

- Namespace governance with ResourceQuota and LimitRange
- Namespace-scoped RBAC and ServiceAccounts
- Lightweight CI gates using kubectl/yq
- Local validation vs CI parity

Code Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  kubectl -n "$ns" get resourcequota >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing ResourceQuota in $ns"; exit 1; }
  kubectl -n "$ns" get limitrange >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing LimitRange in $ns"; exit 1; }
  for dep in $(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {/end}'); do
    sa=$(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy "$dep" -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName}')
    if [ -z "$sa" ]; then echo "Deployment $dep in $ns uses default SA"; exit 1; fi
    kubectl -n "$ns" get rolebinding | grep -q "$sa" || { echo "Missing RBAC for $sa in $ns"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

Failing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: rq
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    limits.cpu: "8"
    requests.memory: 8Gi
    limits.memory: 16Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: lr
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  limits:
  - max:
      cpu: "4"
      memory: 8Gi
    min:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a-view
  namespace: team-a
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: view
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: sa-team-a
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.21
```

Verification

- Locally: run the gate script against your cluster context and verify it fails/passes as expected; inspect output for missing quota/limitrange or RBAC gaps.
- CI: run the same script in a workflow step; ensure failing manifests fail the build and passing manifests pass.
